identity_note: Proposed research-record id only. Not a BCS, BCE, or BCR identity.
title: Aldessa consent inside the early Roanoke guide
type: Historical creative technique. Supplement, not a second missing-colony record.
context: Early Roanoke guide, BCS-000137. Collaborative source.
references: sources/roanoke/BCS-000137/source.md line 58. Line 536 names Aldessa in a later dream and was not used.
supported_facts: Line 58 says Aldessa has given permission to kill off her character, asks collaborators to endear people to her before she dies tragically, and says the writer is looking to pull heart strings. It considers asking her to reveal a pregnancy or a child in the village.
interpretation: The researcher read this as a scripted tragic beat that can constrain agency, beside a fixed missing-colony premise. This row keeps only the consent sentence. It does not restate the missing-colony, burial, or red-herring findings.
confidence: DIRECT for that sentence. Catalog authorship of BCS-000137 is UNKNOWN. The guide names co-DMs and signs itself as a dev team. First person was not upgraded.
scope: EVENT_SPECIFIC. The researcher's CAMPAIGN_SPECIFIC scope is not adopted for this supplement.
alternatives: The planned death may not have been played. Permission in a prep note is not a record of the player's later experience.
limitations: Open draft PR #48 W4-20261016-002 already cites lines 8–68 of this file for the precommitted fate and the unfinished burning branch. Line 58 sits in that window and was not extracted there. Not independent confirmation of W4-002.
kit_applicability: None from this row. A consent sentence is not a license to kill a player character.
exclusions: Do not kill a player character from this note. Do not treat the sentence as Brendon's sole authorship. Do not use line 536 as support.
strengthening_evidence: A played scene and a participant account of the permission.
evaluation: Separate a prepared emotional consequence from a player-contingent result and from explicit permission. The researcher asked for that separation. This file does not perform it.
overlap: PR #48 W4-20261016-002 and W4-20261016-005. W4-005 is the NPC-cast claim, not this consent sentence.

title: Impaired speech as a cooperative NPC affordance
context: Roanoke Season 3, 2020-08-21, channel hex-n-outskirts-of-new-roanoke. Not the out-of-character fight channel.
supported_facts: Brendon presents rustling, then Flivver hiding poorly, then halting Common, and an out-of-character note that the NPC is trying to speak Common. In the same channel, Copper waves and says hello friend (746255459660464159, 746255721653600367). Web offers that Flivver can speak woodland arcanian (746255555122692186) and introduces him (746255622042943489). Copper asks what Flivver is asking them to do (746256944788013112). Baeshra says Baeshra think want go with (746257181783097385). Web says they can meet Ohma and starts walking (746257398942924821, 746257450067558481). Brendon then marks an escort quest accepted. The words escort quest are his out-of-character line, not a player's.
interpretation: The researcher: a communication constraint generated real exchange instead of acting as a generic NPC voice effect. This pass did not replace that reading. The exchange is written chat, not audio.
confidence: DIRECT for the cited lines. EVENT_SPECIFIC.
scope: EVENT_SPECIFIC. Same calendar day and same shard file as BJ-004. Different channel and different claim. Not an independent sample of another session.
alternatives: Players already knew Flivver. Web's introduction does part of the work. Success is this stretch of chat, not a general dialogue method.
limitations: File-neighbor rows are other channels and are not this scene. The fight discussion in channel 636012145204527127 is BJ-004 and was not folded in. No voice or accent evidence.
kit_applicability: Candidate example of a language barrier that stays interpretable. Not approved for use.
exclusions: Do not use this to simulate a speech disability for humor. Do not make every NPC cryptic. Do not treat the scene as proof of spoken performance.
strengthening_evidence: Other attributable Brendon NPC conversations, including flat or stalled ones, and any voice session.
evaluation: The researcher asked to compare limits that create an interpretable goal with garbling that hides a necessary fact. That comparison was not run.
overlap: Same date as open PR #43 BJ-004. Not the same messages and not merged into that record.

title: Authorship exclusions are not personal expertise
type: Negative provenance caution. Not a DM trait.
context: Containers the researcher flagged so they would not be imported as Brendon's individual style.
references: BCS-000141 metadata, sources/empire-city/BCS-000141/. BCS-000195 metadata. BCS-000067 source.md line 8. BCS-000017 catalog authorship. BCS-000180 and BCS-000186 catalog authorship.
supported_facts: BCS-000141 authorship basis says the Drive owner and last modifier are Anthony S, not Brendon Faulkner. Catalog status remains UNKNOWN. BCS-000195 basis says file search reports the owner as darknessemerald. Catalog status remains UNKNOWN. BCS-000067 line 8 is an assistant self-prompt beginning 'Here's a self-prompt designed to guide me when assisting you'. Catalog status remains UNKNOWN. BCS-000017, BCS-000180, and BCS-000186 are UNKNOWN. Ownership or conception is not sentence authorship. BCS-000017's emotional description in the report was not re-audited.
interpretation: The researcher: importing these wholesale as individual style would teach authorial misattribution. This row agrees only as a filter. It does not decide that Brendon never directed a passage.
confidence: DIRECT for the metadata bases and for the BCS-000067 opening. No general DM trait.
scope: Provenance safeguard for these containers. Not CROSS_CAMPAIGN practice.
alternatives: He may have directed or approved some passages. These fields do not prove that either way.
limitations: This caution does not remove collaborator material from the game's fictional world. It only refuses to treat it as Brendon's demonstrated performance.
exclusions: Do not discard collaborator-derived world material as in-world fact. Do not treat BCS-000067 as Brendon's self-description. Open draft PR #48 W4-20261016-014 already excludes that self-prompt from the At War's End comparison.
evaluation: A character monologue from these containers does not, by itself, demonstrate Brendon's performance.
overlap: Catalog and metadata are the authorship authority. This row does not override them. W4-20261016-014 and W4-20261016-016 already bound BCS-000067 and BCS-000180.
